title: QUIZ - 95
description: Test your knowledge, strengthen your reasoning, and learn something new with every question.

questions.concept: Using a Graph's Model to Predict Values
questions.learningObjective: Use a graphed linear model's equation to predict a value at a given input
questions.question: A graph models delivery cost as a straight line with slope 25 and y-intercept 82. What does the graph predict the cost will be for 14 deliveries?
questions.explanation: The model is cost = 25x + 82. At x = 14: 25(14) + 82 = 432.
questions.hint: Use the graph's slope-intercept model to compute the predicted value at the given input.

questions.concept: Using Graph Models to Find Break-Even Points
questions.learningObjective: Use two graphed cost models to find their break-even (equal-cost) point
questions.question: Two services have cost models \(C_A=14x+54\) and \(C_B=6x+91\). At what nonnegative value of \(x\) do the models have the same cost?
questions.explanation: Set the models equal: \(14x+54=6x+91\). Then \(8x=37\), so \(x=\frac{37}{8}\).
questions.hint: Set the two cost models equal and solve for the nonnegative intersection value of \(x\).

questions.concept: Using Graph Models to Find Break-Even Points
questions.learningObjective: Use two graphed cost models to find their break-even (equal-cost) point
questions.question: Two services model cost as graphs: Service A: C = 12x + 64, Service B: C = 19x + 50. Using these models, at what number of units x do the two services cost the same?
questions.explanation: Set the models equal: 12x + 64 = 19x + 50. Solving: (12-19)x = -14, so x = 2.
questions.hint: Set the two cost models equal to each other and solve for x, which is where their graphs would intersect.

questions.concept: Reading Inputs from a Computational Graph Model
questions.learningObjective: Use a graphed model's equation to find the input corresponding to a target output
questions.question: A graph models total cost as C = 9x + 41. According to this model, how many units (x) correspond to a total cost of $158?
questions.explanation: Set 9x + 41 = 158. Subtracting 41: 9x = 117. Dividing by 9: x = 13.
questions.hint: Set the model's formula equal to the target value and solve for x, just as you would read the corresponding point off the graph.
